newsitem.title: MEXICO: Key Mexican Cetes rate breaks downward trend.
newsitem.headline: Key Mexican Cetes rate breaks downward trend.

text.p: Mexico's bellwether one-month Cetes rate broke a three-week decline to rise slightly at Banco de Mexico's primary treasury bill auction on Monday.

Analysts said the increase was mainly due to nervousness over the direction of interest rates in the United States after a speech last week by the chairman of the U.S. Federal Reserve Board who spoke of "irrational exuberance" in some markets.
The widespread market volatility that followed carried over to this week.

"It was a result of the statements by (Federal Reserve Board chairman Alan) Greenspan, which caused nervousness that he might be giving a signal that interest rates could increase in the U.S.," said Santander Investments economist Enrique Ramirez.
Rates also rose on expectations that inflation could come in relatively high in November, analysts said.
However, in a report that came out after the auction on Monday, Banco de Mexico said that the consumer price index rose 1.52 percent in November from the month before.
That was at the low end of expectations.
At the auction this week the rate on the one-month paper rose 27 basis points to 27.29 percent, which was also below expectations.
A survey of 10 Cetes dealers earlier in the day found expectations of a rise of 83 basis points on the one-month paper.
"The reaction was very moderate, which shows the stability of Mexican markets," said Ramirez.
Demand also fell this week to 11.39 billion pesos compared with 12.81 billion pesos the week before, although foreign investors were seen moderating rate rises.
At the primary auction, the rate on the three-month paper rose 51 basis points to 26.57 percent, while six-month paper showed a decline of five basis points to 25.76 percent.
The yield on one-year paper this week was 25.59 percent compared to 25.46 percent a week before.
The auction was held a day earlier than normal to take into account a market holiday in Mexico on Thursday.
